q: According to Newton's second law, F = ma = m(v-v₀)/t, where another important physical quantity is the product of mass and _____.
e: The product of mass and velocity is momentum, an important physical quantity in mechanics.

q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity, which is written as p=_____.
e: Momentum is defined as p = mv, the product of mass and velocity.

q: Momentum of a body is directly proportional to its _____.
e: Momentum is directly proportional to velocity (p = mv).
Momentum is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of _____.
e: Since p = mv, the direction of momentum is the same as the direction of velocity.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the product of mass unit and velocity unit. In MKS system it is kg m s⁻_____.
e: The unit of momentum in MKS system is kg m s⁻¹.

q: The law of conservation of momentum states that: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is _____.
e: The law of conservation of momentum states that total momentum remains constant in an isolated system with no net external force.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both macroscopic and _____ objects.
e: Conservation of momentum applies to both macroscopic (large) and microscopic (small) objects.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, total momentum before collision = total momentum _____ collision.
e: The law states that total momentum before collision equals total momentum after collision.

q: In mathematical form, conservation of momentum for two bodies is: m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + _____, where primed velocities are after collision.
e: The conservation equation is: m_A v_A + m_B v_B = m_A v'_A + m_B v'_B.

q: In the conservation of momentum equation, v_A and v_B are velocities of the masses _____ collision.
e: v_A and v_B (without primes) represent velocities before collision.

q: In the conservation of momentum equation, v'_A and v'_B are velocities of the masses _____ collision.
e: v'_A and v'_B (with primes) represent velocities after collision.

q: When a compressed spring between two wooden balls is released, according to conservation of momentum, if total initial momentum is zero, the final total momentum will also be _____.
e: If initial total momentum is zero, conservation of momentum requires final total momentum to also be zero.

q: When two balls are pushed apart by a compressed spring, m_B v'_B = -m_A v'_A. The minus sign indicates that the two velocity vectors are parallel but _____ in direction.
e: The negative sign indicates the velocities are in opposite directions.

q: By using the relation m_B v'_B = m_A v'_A (taking magnitudes only), inertial _____ can be measured.
e: This relation from conservation of momentum can be used to measure inertial mass.
